dedupe_keys.name: horizon cpt based liquefaction risk assessment and decision software

description: Horizon: CPT-based liquefaction risk assessment and decision software is a dataset listed in DesignSafe Data Depot (published projects), a research data repository for natural hazards engineering under the section "other", published or maintained by Brett Maurer, University of Washington (washington.edu). Horizon is windows-executable software for analyzing the occurence, consequence, mitigation, and economics of seismically-induced soil liquefaction via CPT sensing and models. Features include: (1) CPT processing: Inverse filtering and interface correction; CPT sensor alignment via statistical cross-correlation. (2) Six triggering models; Four free-field manifestation models; Shallow-foundation fragility and vulnerability models. Coverage: as described in the project (site or event named in the description). DesignSafe files it as a "other" project. Its DOI is 10.17603/ds2-2fky-tm46. Keywords: liquefaction, CPT, software, triggering, manifestation, fragility. Published 2020-06-25. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is GPL-3.0. Caveats: this record was written from the catalogue listing only, so the linked page was not opened, its contents and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support structural performance, hazard exposure and resilience studies. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-designsafe-data-depot-repository.
